brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.
requirements.evidence: The spike is placed at the junction of cells (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0) (spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0), on the corner shared by those cells. A drawer in any cell holding that corner is refused: a drawer on the half-base cut face at (1,0) key w and at (0,0) key e both return SPIKE_CLASH ('a spike stands at a corner of this cell the drawer would fill. Take the spike off first'). The configurator will not seat a drawer and a spike at the same corner, so I did not build that pairing. The drawer was not added.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner of a cell
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 stands where three cells meet, on half-w (0,0), full (1,-1), half-e (1,0).

finish.summary: I could build the spike but not the drawer at the same corner. The configurator refuses any drawer whose half-cell contains the spike's corner (SPIKE_CLASH), so the requested pairing cannot be built. The current build is a three-cell junction with one spike, end caps on open faces and joints locked. One LOOSE_BODY warning remains on the half-e base; it is a warning, not a rule error, and the mesh check reads clear. Drawers do place elsewhere (e.g. on a half-base cut face away from the spike), but that would not meet the same-corner requirement.
